response: Mucosal redundancy is a constant associated finding in infants with hypertrophic pyloric stenosis (IHPS). Although the origin of the redundancy and a cause-and-effect relationship are difficult to establish, research suggests that hypergastrinemia may be implicated in the pathogenesis of IHPS. Additionally, mucosal thickening could be implicated as one of the initiating factors in the development of IHPS, supporting the hypothesis that there may be an etiologic role in the in vivo visualization of pyloric mucosal hypertrophy in infants with hypertrophic pyloric stenosis.
